To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we observed differentially expressed proteins and metabolites after exposure to AgNMs and AgNO3.
Silver nanomaterials caused more upregulated proteins/metabolites than silver ions and the impact on proteins/metabo-lites was clearly larger at the end of the experiment.
the molecular responses to Ag NM300K and Ag NO3 were clearly different and that the impact of the NMs on proteins and metabolites was higher at the lower concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating mechanisms of toxicity of AgNMs and ions, which will be used for future development of mechanistically based models.
the elucidation of the underlying mechanisms of AgNMs toxicity, and we show that HTP techniques are useful tools in this respect.
the identification of molecular events in a model organism, which may be used to predict the effects in more complex organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AgNMs cause a more complex response than Ag+ ions.
the apical effects are the consequence of a complex network of interactions, which are differentially activated in a dose-dependent manner by AgNO3 and NM300K.
NM300K and Ag ions cause similar but different effects, with the NM being more toxic.

we have added a large number of key events in AOPs and we have shown that metabolomics and proteomics are useful to assess the underlying molecular mechanisms that precede phenotypic effects.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of HTP technologies in combination with the AOP framework can be a powerful tool in the elucidation of the underlying mechanisms in nanomaterials toxicity.
the underlying molecular mechanisms of AgNMs and Ag ions can be assessed by multiomics approaches and that the apical observed effect can be explained by the underlying mechanisms.
